overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation in the February 18 minutes omitting supporting documents, and declined to review the City Solicitor-conduct and settlement-detail allegations.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the City Solicitor refused to let the Council ask questions about a request to appropriate settlement funds at the February 18 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law applies to public bodies and individuals acting as public body members, it does not apply to municipal employees.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Council failed to discuss the appropriation of settlement funds in sufficient detail at the February 18 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any topic, nor does it establish requirements for the level of detail a public body’s discussions must include.

allegations.summary: Alleged the February 18 minutes failed to list backup or supporting documents used for the settlement funding request.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent the complaint alleges that the “backup” or “supporting” documents were used during the February 18 meeting and therefore should have been listed in the meeting minutes, we find that they were not.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
